# Install on Windows from a clean checkout

## What's bundled

* Python source (no compiled artefacts; everything is generated by `scripts\train.bat`)
* Pinned `requirements.txt`
* Windows `.bat` scripts with CRLF line endings
* `catboost_info/` is excluded from the repo (CatBoost writes it during training)
* `.dockerignore` slims the Docker context

## Install Python (if missing)

1. Python 3.12 (3.10-3.12 are supported; 3.13+ is NOT supported by the pinned packages) from <https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/>
2. Tick **Add Python to PATH**
3. Verify: in a fresh `cmd` window run `python --version`

## System dependencies (PRD §4.9 hint)

* `lightgbm` wheels ship with their native deps. On Windows you may also need the **Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable 2015–2022** if a third-party package error mentions a missing native lib. Download: <https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe>
* On Linux the `python:3.12-slim` Dockerfile already installs `libgomp1`; check `aws/deploy_notes.md` §5.

## One-time setup

```
scripts\setup_windows.bat
```

This creates `.venv\` and installs everything in `requirements.txt`. Re-run only if you blow away `.venv`.

## Train the model

```
scripts\train.bat
```

This:
1. Trains all six algorithms with stratified cross-validation
2. Logs every run + the best model to MLflow (`mlruns/`) and registers it as `purchase-intent-best`
3. Runs the **PageValues ablation** and writes `reports\pagevalues_ablation.json`
4. Writes global SHAP, permutation-importance PNG, LIME HTML
5. Writes the model card `reports\MODEL_CARD.md`

Outputs:

```
models\best_model.joblib
models\preprocessing_pipeline.joblib
models\decision_threshold.json
models\training_metadata.json
reports\MODEL_CARD.md
reports\explainability_summary.json
reports\pagevalues_ablation.json
reports\lime_local_session0.html
reports\figures\shap_global_summary.png
reports\figures\permutation_importance.png
mlruns\...                      (MLflow experiment + registered model)
```

## Run the API and dashboard

```
scripts\run_all.bat
```

This opens both services in two windows:

| URL | Service |
|---|---|
| <http://127.0.0.1:8000/health> | FastAPI health |
| <http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict> | Predictions (POST) |
| <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> | Interactive Swagger UI |
| <http://127.0.0.1:8501> | Streamlit dashboard |

## Inspect the MLflow run

```
scripts\run_mlflow.bat
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:5000>; you should see the experiment `purchase-intent` with a parent run `cv-benchmark` (6 nested per-model runs) and a final run `BEST-CatBoost` (or whichever model won).

## Tests and quality

```
scripts\test.bat      REM pytest
scripts\lint.bat      REM black + ruff
```

## Docker alternative (if Docker Desktop is installed)

```
docker compose up --build
```

Brings up api, dashboard and MLflow UI. Note: `docker compose up` starts the `train` service first and retrains the model before the API starts (a few minutes).

**Verification status:** on Windows with Docker Desktop 4.94 (Docker 29.8.2), all three images built successfully and the `api`, `dashboard` and `mlflow` services were started with `docker compose up -d --no-deps api dashboard mlflow`, using the pre-trained artefacts in `models\` and `reports\`. `/health`, `/predict`, the dashboard and the MLflow UI were checked. The `train` service inside Docker (a full `docker compose up --build`) was **not** run.
